title: Pointwise compact bounded coherent diagrams are compact in their functor category
statement:
Use the universes $\mathcal U\in\mathcal U'$, $\kappa$-smallness, $\kappa$-filteredness and $\kappa$-compactness of [def-coef-presentable-infinity-category], coherent functor categories, mapping spaces and colimits of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], and pointwise functor-category colimits of [lem-coef-infinity-yoneda-presheaf-limits]. Let $\kappa\in\mathcal U$ be an infinite regular cardinal, let $\mathcal C$ be a locally small quasicategory fitting in $\mathcal U'$ and admitting all small $\kappa$-filtered colimits, and let $K$ be a $\kappa$-small simplicial set. If $a:K\to\mathcal C$ has $\kappa$-compact value at every vertex, then $a$ is a $\kappa$-compact object of $\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal C)$. Explicitly, for every small $\kappa$-filtered quasicategory $I$, coherent diagram $D:I\to\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal C)$ and colimiting coherent cocone $D\to\Delta_I b$, the cocone
$$\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal C)}(a,D(-))\longrightarrow\Delta_I\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal C)}(a,b)$$
obtained by postcomposition with that cocone is colimiting in $\mathcal S_{\mathcal U'}$. The target diagrams $D(i)$ and $b$ are arbitrary and need not be constant on $K$. The case $K=\varnothing$ is included.

source.place: Proposition 5.3.4.13, printed pp.399-401 (PDF pp.416-418), with Definition 5.3.4.5, printed p.396, and pointwise colimits Corollary 5.1.2.3, printed p.319. Read online 2026-10-17; not archived in literature/. No Stacks tag states this quasicategorical theorem.

proof.text: Put $H=\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal C)$. The coherent functor construction in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones] makes $H$ a quasicategory, and [lem-coef-functor-spine-tower-mapping-descent] gives its local smallness and identifies mapping spaces with the coherent restriction limits used below. Let $I$ be a small $\kappa$-filtered quasicategory and let $D:I\to H$ have a colimiting cocone with apex $b$. Since $\mathcal C$ has the required filtered colimits, [lem-coef-infinity-yoneda-presheaf-limits] computes this cocone objectwise: for every vertex $v$ of $K$, the cocone $D(i)(v)\to b(v)$ is colimiting in $\mathcal C$. We will compare the mapping-space cocone for $a$ with these vertexwise colimits.

For a standard simplex $\Delta^n$, prove by induction on $n$ that a diagram $a:\Delta^n\to\mathcal C$ whose vertex values are $\kappa$-compact has mapping space out of $a$ commuting with the given $I$-colimit. The case $n=0$ is the vertex compactness hypothesis. For $n=1$, [lem-coef-infinity-arrow-morphism-square] identifies the mapping space with a homotopy pullback of the two endpoint mapping spaces over the intervening mapping space; [lem-coef-spaces-kappa-limit-filtered-colimit] interchanges this finite homotopy limit with the $I$-colimit, and naturality identifies the resulting comparison with postcomposition by the given cocone. For $n>1$, let $S_0=\Delta^{\{0\}}$ and, for $0\leq j<n$, let $S_{j+1}$ be the union of the first $j+1$ consecutive spine edges and their vertices. The spine equivalence in [lem-coef-functor-spine-tower-mapping-descent] identifies mapping spaces for $a$ with those for $a|_{S_n}=a|_{\operatorname{Sp}[n]}$. For each $j$, $S_{j+1}=S_j\amalg_{\Delta^{\{j\}}}\Delta^{\{j,j+1\}}$, where the vertex inclusion is degreewise injective; [lem-coef-infinity-mapping-excision] therefore expresses the mapping space for $S_{j+1}$ as a homotopy pullback of the spaces for $S_j$ and that edge over the common vertex. Induction on $j$, the already proved $n=1$ case for the edge, and the spaces lemma give the filtered-colimit comparison at every stage. Thus the comparison from the colimit of the mapping-space diagram to the mapping space into $b$ is an equivalence, including its coherent cocone maps.

For $m\geq-1$ let $P(m)$ assert that every $\kappa$-small simplicial set $L$ of dimension at most $m$, with a diagram having $\kappa$-compact vertex values, is $\kappa$-compact in $\operatorname{Fun}(L,\mathcal C)$, with the actual postcomposition cocone maps. Step 1 lets us apply this assertion to restrictions of the given cocone. For $m=-1$, $L=\varnothing$, the functor category and all mapping spaces are terminal, so the empty-shape clause of [lem-coef-spaces-kappa-limit-filtered-colimit] proves $P(-1)$. Assume $P(n-1)$ and let $L$ have dimension at most $n$. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-monomorphism-boundary-cells] to $L_{n-1}\hookrightarrow L=L_n$. There are no new cells below dimension $n$ or above dimension $n$, so its filtration has just one nontrivial attachment: the pushout of one copy of $\partial\Delta^n\hookrightarrow\Delta^n$ for each nondegenerate $n$-simplex of $L$. The family of cells is $\kappa$-small because $L$ is $\kappa$-small.

source.place: Proposition 5.3.4.13, proof of (4)--(5), with the skeletal attachment supplied by the cited Mathlib leaf

proof.text: For the pushout in Step 3, write $A_n=\coprod_\sigma\partial\Delta^n$ and $E_n=\coprod_\sigma\Delta^n$. The mapping spaces on $A_n$ and $E_n$ are the products of the mapping spaces on their cells, by the defining formulas of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]: for $J=\coprod_\sigma J_\sigma$ one has $J\times\Delta^m=\coprod_\sigma(J_\sigma\times\Delta^m)$ degreewise, so restriction gives an isomorphism of simplicial sets $\operatorname{Fun}(J,\mathcal C)\cong\prod_\sigma\operatorname{Fun}(J_\sigma,\mathcal C)$, compatible with operators; an $m$-simplex $\Delta^{m+1}\to\prod_\sigma\operatorname{Fun}(J_\sigma,\mathcal C)$ of a right-pinched mapping space is a family of such simplices with the endpoint conditions imposed componentwise, so the mapping space is the product of Kan complexes of the component mapping spaces, naturally in both diagrams (terminal for an empty family). Each simplex cell is covered by Step 2, while every boundary and $L_{n-1}$ has dimension at most $n-1$ and is covered by $P(n-1)$. The comparison for the pushout is the homotopy pullback supplied by [lem-coef-infinity-mapping-excision]. The spaces lemma [lem-coef-spaces-kappa-limit-filtered-colimit] commutes with the $\kappa$-small products and the finite pullback, naturally in the target diagram. Hence the filtered-colimit comparison is an equivalence for $L_n$, proving $P(n)$. Induction gives the claim for every finite-dimensional $\kappa$-small simplicial set.

For arbitrary $K$, write $K=\bigcup_{n\ge0}\operatorname{sk}_nK$. If $\kappa=\aleph_0$, then $K$ has only finitely many nondegenerate simplices, hence bounded dimension, so it is one of the finite-dimensional cases of Step 4. If $\kappa>\aleph_0$, the indexing nerve $N(\mathbb N^{\mathrm{op}})$ is $\kappa$-small. The tower clause of [lem-coef-functor-spine-tower-mapping-descent] identifies the mapping space out of $a$ with the homotopy limit of the mapping spaces out of its skeleta. Each skeleton comparison is an equivalence by Step 4, and [lem-coef-spaces-kappa-limit-filtered-colimit] interchanges this $\kappa$-small homotopy limit with the $I$-filtered colimit. Hence the comparison cocone for $a$ is colimiting. If $K=\varnothing$, the defining formula gives $\operatorname{Fun}(K,\mathcal C)=\Delta^0$ and all relevant mapping spaces are terminal; their filtered colimit is terminal by the empty-shape clause of the same spaces lemma.

theorem pointwise_compact_diagrams
    (κ : Cardinal.{u}) (hκ : κ.IsRegular)
    (C : SSet.{max (u + 1) v}) [Quasicategory C]
    (hClocal : IsLocallySmall.{u, max (u + 1) v} C)
    (hCcolim : HasSmallKappaFilteredColimits C κ)
    (K : SSet.{max (u + 1) v}) (hK : IsKappaSmall κ K)
    (a : K ⟶ C)
    (ha : ∀ k : K _⦋0⦌, IsKappaCompact C κ (a.app (op ⦋0⦌) k)) :
    IsKappaCompact ((ihom K).obj C) κ (SSet.Enhanced.diagramVertex a)
